summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with Type 1 diabetes and a history of gastroparesis was admitted for intractable nausea and vomiting, unable to tolerate oral intake. She was managed with IV fluids, antiemetics including Reglan as a substitute for non-formulary domperidone, and insulin therapy with D5W to address urinary ketones. Her hypertension was controlled with IV metoprolol initially, then transitioned to oral medications. She gradually advanced her diet, tolerating a full meal by discharge. A chest X-ray showed no new abnormalities, and urine culture indicated contamination without infection. Porphyria testing was negative, though pheochromocytoma evaluation was incomplete due to non-compliance with urine collection. She was discharged home on her prior medications with follow-up scheduled with her GI physician.
problems: Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
